models_evaluated: 10 state-of-the-art LLMs (including open-weight models; specific names not reported in text)

links.outcome: Benchmark versus end-to-end logical consistency of LLMs in risk-of-bias assessment
links.effect: Top model reached 98.88% Atomic Consistency but end-to-end consistency collapsed to 45.13%; several open-weight models fell to nearly 0%.
links.quote: Experiments on 10 state-of-the-art LLMs reveal a catastrophic Error Compounding Effect: despite the top model reaching 98.88% Atomic Consistency, its end-to-end consistency collapses to 45.13%, with several open-weight architectures plummeting to nearly 0%.

links.outcome: Failure to deduce correct outcomes from retrieved evidence and blind guess rates
links.effect: Even with high-quality evidence retrieved, models failed to deduce correct outcomes in 18.63-40.05% of cases; Blind Guess Rates reached 48.28%.
links.quote: We further uncover a systematic evidence-reasoning gap: even when models retrieve high-quality evidence, they fail to deduce correct outcomes in 18.63-40.05% of cases, while Blind Guess Rates reach 48.28%.

unlisted_practices: White-box hierarchical logical consistency verification of LLM reasoning against expert logic (Cochrane RoB 2.0)

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM reasoning consistency and evidence-reasoning gap on a Risk of Bias (RoB 2.0) benchmark of RCTs, but does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
